prerequisites: Solid knowledge of the content of the courses Higher Mathematics 1 to Higher Mathematics 3
Basic programming skills in C++ and MATLAB®

learning_outcomes.text: Students understand the concept of a signal in all its forms and know what a linear time-invariant system is. They can name practical examples.

Students know the different representation forms for Linear Time-Invariant Systems in both analog and digital form and are able to transform the representation forms into one another. They can differentiate the information resulting from the representation forms and explain the resulting benefit.

Students master the most important signal transformations and can apply them both analytically and by simulation using MATLAB. They can explain the meaning of the transformations and illustrate them with examples.
They are able to question, evaluate, and analyze corresponding graphical representations.

Students have knowledge of the forms of description of the transfer behavior of Linear Time-Invariant Systems in the time, image, and frequency domain and can state the relationships and convert the description forms into one another. They can illustrate the differences to nonlinear systems with examples.
Students know the central result of Shannon's sampling theorem and can identify and assign the associated phenomena.

Students know how the concepts of deterministic signal theory can be transferred to stochastic signals and can explain the differences. They can apply the corresponding results in laboratory experiments from a digital signal processor and correctly interpret the experimental results.

syllabus_topics: Description and analysis of analog signals and systems
Linear time-invariant systems (LTI systems) in the time domain
The convolution integral
The Laplace transform, description of LTI systems in the image domain
Special system excitation signals, the Dirac impulse
The impulse response of an LTI system
Amplitude and phase response of an LTI system
The Fourier transform, LTI systems in the frequency domain
Concept of the spectrum
Properties and calculation rules of the Fourier transform
Sampling and digitization
The sampling process, approximation with sampling impulses
Impulse sampling and sampling spectrum
Relationship between Fourier spectrum and sampling spectrum
Problem of reconstructibility, spectral overlap
Description and analysis of digital signals and systems
Description of digital LTI systems
Digital LTI systems in the time domain
The discrete convolution
The Z-transform, description of LTI systems in the image domain
Pole-zero diagrams, stability of discrete-time systems
The impulse response of a digital LTI system
Digital LTI systems in the frequency domain
The Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT, FFT)
Aliasing and Leakage
Transmission properties of digital LTI systems
FIR and IIR filters, FIR approximation of the ideal low-pass filter
IIR filter design - Butterworth filter example
Application of the content taught in the lecture on a real Embedded System
Digitization of analog sensor data
Creation of a real-time system
UDP data transmission
Signal processing using FFT
Digital filters (FIR or IIR)
Signal processing in MATLAB®

assessment_methods.method: Written, graded examination (Klausur) of 90 minutes or oral examination of 20 minutes
Laboratory with ungraded lab reports as study achievement
